recommended.title: Playback session API
recommended.acceptance: Server resolves authorized provider candidates and clients cannot submit arbitrary media URLs; the session response is a discriminated union on outcome (granted, denied, unavailable) with reasons present on every branch rather than as an optional field, because a denial with no reason trail violates the reason-trail invariant exactly as much as a grant with none

recommended.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
recommended.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
recommended.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
recommended.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

recommended.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
recommended.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
recommended.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
recommended.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. A native error can be represented without borrowing a Shaka code and without discarding the detail the engine did supply. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.
